input.quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
input.rationale:
The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall payment or volume cap on the Company. The sole compensation to HDI (§ 3.1) is a pure revenue share — 30% of Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly threshold — so the Company pays only on actual sales achieved and owes nothing if the Site generates no revenue; the $11,000 figure is a floor below which no fee accrues, which benefits us rather than functioning as a minimum spend. There is no guaranteed hosting volume or committed order quantity anywhere in the document (searches for "minimum", "commit", "volume" return nothing on point). The term is a one-year term with annual auto-renewal terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (§ 4.1), so we also have a standing exit. This meets the preferred position (fees for usage/ordered services only).

Two adjacent terms noted but not deviations under this rule: (i) the Termination Payment in § 4.2 is an exit fee calculated as half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000 — it is triggered by, and scales with, actual sales rather than by any purchase shortfall, and it is expressly zero where the formula yields zero or less, so it is not a take-or-pay penalty (any concern with its size belongs to the termination-fee rule, not here); and (ii) the § 6.1 exclusivity restricts the Company from running a similar Deerskin Products site elsewhere, which is a channel/exclusivity restriction rather than a volume commitment and is properly addressed under the exclusivity rule.
